does: Cooks delicate food gently in liquid that is hot but never boils.

intro.what: Poaching cooks delicate food in gently heated liquid without a rolling boil.
intro.why: It teaches you to control liquid movement so that delicate food is not knocked about.

how: Heat the liquid until it trembles, with small bubbles on the bottom of the pan and almost none rising.
Hold the heat there. Turn it down the moment bubbles start to break the surface.
Lift the food out with a slotted spoon and drain it well.
For an egg, add a little vinegar to the water, crack the egg into a small bowl first, and tip it in at the surface.
For dumplings of choux paste, drop spoonfuls into salted water at a tremble, and lift them out with a slotted spoon once they float and feel firm.

cues.text: The surface shivers and steams, and nothing rolls.
A poached egg feels like a soft cushion when pressed: the white is set and the yolk is loose inside.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the liquid boil, which tears an egg apart and toughens fish and chicken.
mistakes.fix: Turn the heat down, or add a splash of cold liquid.

mistakes.mistake: Using an old egg, whose thin white spreads into rags.
mistakes.fix: Use the freshest eggs you have, and drain off the watery part of the white through a sieve.

quiz.question: Why does this method keep the liquid from boiling?
choices: To use movement in the water to keep the food from breaking.
To stop the liquid from losing any volume.
quiz.because: Boiling can tear delicate food apart. Gentle liquid movement treats it more softly.

quiz.question: How do you add food to the poaching liquid?
choices: Tip the food in with a quick splash to separate the pieces.
Stir it rapidly into a rolling boil.
quiz.because: Slide the food gently into the liquid instead of splashing it into a rolling boil.

quiz.question: Which surface matches the gentle liquid heat used for poaching?
choices: A rolling surface with large breaking bubbles.
A still, cold surface without steam.
A shivering, steaming surface that does not roll.
quiz.because: A shivering, steaming surface without rolling bubbles shows the gentle liquid movement used here.

quiz.question: The liquid starts boiling after the food goes in. What should you change?
choices: Turn the heat down or add a splash of cold liquid.
Turn the heat up to maintain the rolling boil.
Stir harder to keep the bubbles moving.
quiz.because: Lowering the heat or adding a splash of cold liquid brings the liquid back away from a boil.

comes_after.why: Poaching sits just under a simmer, so a cook has to be able to find a simmer first.
